headings.text: A different view for every directory.

images.alt: Illustration of a landscape behind a kitty terminal prompt.

routes.firstParagraph: In development
Kittyscape selects a local background image from your shell’s directory. The active pane in the selected tab controls the image for its OS window, meaning the outer window managed by your desktop.

The development build uses a user-local bundle loaded by kitty. No root privileges, shell framework, system Python package, Node.js runtime, or network image service belongs in the extension’s normal runtime path.

Kittyscape reads kittyscape.json from kitty’s active configuration directory. Rules are shared by every qualified shell in that kitty instance. The file is data only; directory visits never execute project hooks.

Kittyscape uses one kitty-side watcher and the directory reports from kitty’s native shell integration. Bash, Zsh, and Fish share the same resolver and configuration. The current build does not need a separate rules engine or per-prompt helper process in each shell.
Kittyscape selects an image. Kitty remains responsible for layout, interpolation, tint, gap tint, opacity, and theme colors. Changing any of those settings is a separate kitty configuration action.
Start with the tested compatibility rows and the status action. Diagnose an isolated kitty instance before changing a daily-use configuration.

Removal has two parts: restore the running OS windows that Kittyscape still owns, then remove its user-local configuration entry and installed files. A file removal alone cannot restore an already-running window.
0.1.0.dev1 is an experimental local build. MacOS arm64 qualification remains open, as requested. Capability checks and a version floor do not establish support for every intervening release.
The configuration is a JSON object in kittyscape.json, in kitty’s active configuration directory. It is user-owned data. No visited repository is searched for configuration.
The installed configuration exposes lifecycle actions through a local kitty kitten. They apply to OS windows in the current kitty process. Separate kitty processes keep separate state.

Kittyscape is a local development build. The runtime, support matrix, and distribution artifact are qualified together. Publication, hosting, repository ownership, and licensing remain separate decisions.
The local archive and website are being qualified against the product requirements. No package or website has been published, and macOS arm64 qualification remains open.
Experiment and implementation date: September 15, 2026. The release record binds final results to the exact local artifact. MacOS arm64 remains an open qualification gate.

The landing page and documentation are one static VitePress site. Search runs in the browser using a local index. The site makes no analytics, external font, image, or search-service requests. Search queries are not persisted.
The local source bundle and static site are prepared separately from publication. The release record contains immutable artifact identity, the tested matrix, validation results, and open gates.
